question: In a child presenting with chronic liver disease, Wilson disease should be screened for by measuring serum ceruloplasmin (low in Wilson disease) and 24-hour urinary copper (elevated), as this is a treatable cause of chronic liver disease if diagnosed early.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Wilson disease is an important TREATABLE cause of chronic liver disease in children and adolescents. Low serum ceruloplasmin + high 24-h urinary copper + Kayser-Fleischer rings on slit-lamp = diagnostic triad. Liver biopsy copper quantification is the gold standard. Treatment: D-penicillamine/trientine chelation + zinc. Early diagnosis before cirrhosis enables significant clinical improvement.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Wilson disease (autosomal recessive, ATP7B mutation) typically presents between 5–35 years with liver disease, neuropsychiatric features, or both. Serum ceruloplasmin is low (<20 mg/dL), 24-h urine copper is elevated (>100 µg/day; >40 µg/day in children). Kayser-Fleischer rings are seen on slit-lamp. Treatment: D-penicillamine (first-line, chelation) or trientine, plus zinc acetate (blocks copper absorption). It is a treatable cause of CLD — diagnosis before cirrhosis allows reversal of disease.
